title: High-Probability Bounds for the Last Iterate of Clipped SGD
claim: The last iterate of the method converges as fast as or faster than the averaged iterate across diverse objectives, matching theory.
layout: 3 panels in a row, shared legend style, log-scale y-axis with shaded bands
description: Three side-by-side line plots, each showing objective value or error against iteration count k, from 0 to 1000, with a logarithmic y-axis. Each plot compares two curves. Orange is the averaged iterate and green is the last iterate. For each curve, a solid line shows the sample mean, a shaded band shows ±1 standard deviation, and a dotted line shows the 0.95-percentile. The left and right panels show the objective value dropping sharply in the first 100 iterations, then flattening. The green last-iterate curve sits slightly below the orange one. The center panel shows the error falling over several orders of magnitude. The last iterate crosses below the average near k≈100 and ends around 1e-7, while the average stays near 1e-4. Its green band is jagged and stretched at the bottom. Legends sit in the upper right of each panel, and grid lines are light gray.
caption: Experimental results: (left) f(x) = ln(1 + exp(⟨x, a⟩)), (center) f(x) = 1 2∥x∥2, and (right) f(x) = E(Z,Y )∼µ[ln(1 + exp(−Y ⟨x, Z⟩))]. The x-axis shows the iteration counter k, while the y-axis (in logarithmic scale) reports the objective value f(zk) at the iterate zk. Note that in the left and center plots, the y-axis corresponds to the optimization error since infx∈Rd f(x) = 0. In all figures, the dotted line denotes the 0.95-percentile, while the solid line together with the shaded area denotes the sample mean ± one standard deviation. Note that, due to the log scale on the y, the shaded area appears stretched whenever its magnitude differs by orders of magnitude from the sample mean.
abstract: We study the problem of minimizing a convex objective when only noisy gradient estimates are available. Assuming that stochastic gradients have finite $\alpha$-th moments for some $\alpha \in (1,2]$, we establish - for the first time - a high-probability convergence guarantee for the last iterate of clipped stochastic gradient descent (Clipped-SGD) on smooth objectives. In particular, we prove a rate of $1/K^{(2\alpha-2)/(3\alpha)}$ with only polylogarithmic dependence on the confidence parameter. In addition, we introduce a new technique for deriving in-expectation convergence guarantees from high-probability bounds for methods with almost surely bounded updates, and apply it to obtain expectation guarantees for Clipped-SGD. Finally, we complement our theoretical analysis with empirical results that support and illustrate our findings.
